newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest bids expected later this week.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest bids expected later this week.

text.p: At least three bids for TimberWest Forest Ltd were likely to be submitted later this week, one of the lumber producer's directors said on Tuesday.
"We expect multiple bids to come in at the end of this week," said Stephen Bellringer, chief executive of BC Gas and a TimberWest director overseeing the sale.
Asked how many offers were likely, he said in an interview, "We expect more than two. You could say several."
He declined to identify the prospective bidders or speculate on price. Bellringer said there was continued interest in TimberWest from outside Canada.

Among companies rumored to be interested in TimberWest were Avenor Inc, which owns Pacific Forest Products Ltd in British Columbia, Weyerhaeuser Co, Champion International Corp and the timberland investment management division of U.S. insurer John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co.
TimberWest, one of Canada's biggest public companies operating exclusively in logging and lumber, said in October it was putting itself up for sale. Its market capitalization is around C$612 million.

An independent committee of directors would likely meet next week to review the offers and make recommendations to the company's full board before Christmas, Bellringer said. He was uncertain when a deal would be announced.
TimberWest is 52 percent-owned by Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd, which is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd.
The sale effort was prompted by Fletcher Canada's decision to sharpen its focus on its paper business and the view that TimberWest stock was undervalued.

TimberWest has five sawmills in British Columbia with annual capacity of 685 million board feet of lumber. It also has timber tenures with annual harvest of 4.2 million cubic meters of wood including 210,000 hectares of privately owned land on the British Columbia coast.
